title: The 10 Best Corded Shop Vacuums
subtitle: Plug-in wet/dry shop vacs ranked from live Amazon data, from 2.5-gallon car vacs to 16-gallon garage vacs.
intro: A shop vac picks up sawdust, drywall dust, water, and whatever else would wreck a house vacuum. The best-sellers run from 2.5-gallon carry vacs under $50 to 16-gallon garage vacs around $150. We ranked 10 corded wet/dry vacs on rating, review volume, and features (a blower port, a hose 1-7/8 in. or wider, a drain port, and a stainless tank). Every one of them handles both wet and dry pickup.

avoid.name: VEVOR Dry Vacuum Cleaner, 2.6 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Portable Shop Vac, 800W
avoid.flag: Dry-only vac sold as a shop vac
avoid.verdict: It shows up in wet/dry shop vac searches at shop vac prices, but it's a dry-only vacuum. It can't handle the spills and flooded floors most people buy a shop vac for, and the CRAFTSMAN 2.5-gallon does wet, dry, and blowing for about $7 more.
reasons: It's a dry vacuum. The title says "Dry Vacuum Cleaner", the style is listed as "Dry", and its only filter is a dirt separator, with no foam wet filter. Water pickup, the main reason to own a shop vac, is off the table.
The listing can't agree on its own motor: the title says 2.5 peak HP and the first bullet says 2.6 HP.
Its 4 ft hose is the shortest we found, 1 to 3 ft shorter than every vac on the ranked list.
It claims to cover "3.7x more than traditional vacuums" without saying which vacuums or how that was measured.

buyers_guide.q: What does "peak HP" mean on a shop vac?
buyers_guide.a: Peak horsepower is a motor rating measured with no load, and it isn't what you get while vacuuming. It's useful for comparing vacs from the same brand, but airflow (CFM) says more about suction. DEWALT lists 105 CFM for the DXV12P, for example, and Vacmaster lists 70 CFM for the VBVB611PF.

buyers_guide.q: What tank size should I get?
buyers_guide.a: 2.5 to 4 gallons is enough for cars, stairs, and small spills, and those vacs are light enough to carry. 5 to 6 gallons covers most garage and workshop cleanup. Go to 12 to 16 gallons for flooded floors, renovation debris, or a woodshop, and pick one with a drain port so you don't have to lift a full tank of water.

Yes. A 1-1/4 in. hose fits tight spots and car interiors but clogs on wood chips, leaves, and drywall chunks. A 1-7/8 in. or 2-1/2 in. hose moves more air and swallows bigger debris. If you do a lot of workshop cleanup, buy the wider hose.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need to change the filter for wet pickup?
buyers_guide.a: Usually. Most vacs use a paper or cloth cartridge for dry dust and a foam sleeve for water, and running water through a paper cartridge ruins it. Check which filters come in the box: the Vacmaster VOC508S and Amazon Basics both include a foam wet filter.

Stainless tanks resist dents and cost a little more. Poly tanks are lighter, can't rust, and are what most of the bigger vacs use. Both hold water and debris the same way, so choose on size and features first.
